current_law_statement: Reviewed the codified Government Records Access and Management Act (Utah Code Title 63G, Ch. 2) on le.utah.gov as of 2026-08-19, through the 2026 General Session (adjourned March 2026; general effective date 5/6/2026). Fee section § 63G-2-203 is current as amended by Ch. 33 (S.B. 188), 2025 General Session, effective 3/17/2025 — a technical wording change ('requests'→'request') in (8)(a)(ii); its last substantive fee amendment was 2022 (H.B. 96: media-representative definition and the 10-day repeat exception to the free quarter hour). No 2024 (S.B. 240, Ch. 18), 2025 (H.B. 69 Ch. 187; S.B. 277 Ch. 476 creating the Government Records Office; S.B. 188) or 2026 (H.B. 325 Ch. 366 classification; H.B. 425 Ch. 339 'Local Government Fees' — utility/public-safety fees, not records) session law changed any fee figure. § 63G-2-201 was amended in 2026 (effective 7/1/2026) without touching its fee-relevant subsections. Regime: one statute binds all 'governmental entities' incl. political subdivisions; the only numeric parameters are the $50 prepayment trigger and the free first quarter hour; every rate is 'reasonable ... actual cost' set by the political subdivision by ordinance/written policy (§ 63G-2-203(3)(c); § 63G-2-701(3)(c)); state agencies set fees through the budget process/§ 63J-1-504 (§ 63G-2-203(3)(b)) — agency schedules do not bind cities. No Utah Administrative Code rule or AG opinion sets municipal records fees. Guidance-vs-law gap: the Utah Division of Archives and Records Service official forms add (i) that the response time begins on the date prepayment/authorization is provided and (ii) a requester-stated cost-contact amount — neither is in statute.

new_rules.legal_concept: Response time begins on prepayment/authorization (Archives official form)
new_rules.atomic_rule: When a governmental entity requires prepayment or authorization before processing, the response time for processing the request begins on the date the prepayment or authorization is provided (official-form statement).
new_rules.trigger: Entity issues a GRAMA Request for Payment or Prepayment requiring prepayment or authorization
new_rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: response time (10 business days) begins on the date prepayment or authorization is provided (form statement)
new_rules.source_language: Statement about the processing time: The response time for processing this request will begin on the date prepayment, or authorization is provided. Response time is ten business days, but may be longer is extraordinary circumstances apply. | Note: Utah Code § 63G-2-203(1) & (8) provides that a governmental entity may charge a reasonable fee to cover the actual cost of providing a record(s). Prepayment may be required if the cost exceeds $50 or if the requester has not paid for previous requests after an invoice has been sent. Additionally, requesters may ask for a cost estimate before authorizing a governmental entity to process a request.
new_rules.source_authority: Utah Division of Archives and Records Service, 'GRAMA Request for Payment or Prepayment' (2025), p. 2
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Utah Division of Archives and Records Service form, 2025 revision)
new_rules.notes: Guidance-level: the statute (§ 63G-2-203(8)(a)) says only that payment may be required 'before beginning to process a request'; § 63G-2-204(4) does not list prepayment as a tolling event. The form is published for use by any governmental entity. Also states 'requesters may ask for a cost estimate before authorizing a governmental entity to process a request' and 'Additional fees are established by a local ordinance or policy'.

new_rules.legal_concept: Requester-set cost-contact threshold on the official request form
new_rules.atomic_rule: The official GRAMA Request Form lets the requester elect to be contacted if the cost of providing records exceeds an amount the requester states; the official payment form states that requesters may ask for a cost estimate before authorizing processing.
new_rules.trigger: Requester ticks 'contact me if cost exceeds' and states an amount, or asks for a cost estimate
new_rules.source_language: Do you want to be contacted if the cost of providing records exceeds a certain amount? Yes / No. If yes, state the amount | Note: Utah Code § 63G-2-203(1) & (8) provides that a governmental entity may charge a reasonable fee to cover the actual cost of providing a record(s). Prepayment may be required if the cost exceeds $50 or if the requester has not paid for previous requests after an invoice has been sent. Additionally, requesters may ask for a cost estimate before authorizing a governmental entity to process a request.
new_rules.source_authority: Utah Division of Archives and Records Service / Office of the Government Records Ombudsman, 'GRAMA Request Form', p. 2 ('Additional access considerations'); 'GRAMA Request for Payment or Prepayment' (2025), p. 1
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Utah Division of Archives and Records Service form, 2025 revision)
new_rules.notes: Guidance/practice, not law: GRAMA has no estimate-notice threshold. The requester's stated amount is the practical trigger for a cost notice; the payment form's 'The requester authorized a lesser amount. Agreement to pay the total cost is required to process request.' checkbox is the companion outcome.

new_rules.legal_concept: Charge for compiled/reformatted records or non-maintained medium
new_rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity that agrees to compile, format, manipulate, package, summarize, or tailor information, or to provide a record in a format, medium, or program it does not currently maintain, may require the requester to pay for it in accordance with § 63G-2-203.
new_rules.trigger: Requester asks for compilation/tailoring or a non-maintained format/medium and the entity elects to fulfill it (§ 63G-2-201(8)(a)-(b))
new_rules.source_language: (8)(a) Although not required to do so, a governmental entity may, upon request from the person who submitted the records request, compile, format, manipulate, package, summarize, or tailor information or provide a record in a format, medium, or program not currently maintained by the governmental entity. (b) In determining whether to fulfill a request described in Subsection (8)(a), a governmental entity may consider whether the governmental entity is able to fulfill the request without unreasonably interfering with the governmental entity's duties and responsibilities. (c) A governmental entity may require a person who makes a request under Subsection (8)(a) to pay the governmental entity, in accordance with Section 63G-2-203, for providing the information or record as requested.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (63G-2-201 amended 2026 General Session, effective 7/1/2026; fee-related subsections (1)(a), (6), (8)(c), (10) unchanged in substance)
new_rules.notes: Ceiling = actual cost per § 63G-2-203(1)-(2); the (2)(a) component list and the (2)(b) hourly cap apply. Fee-side companion to the no-duty-to-create rule in § 63G-2-201(7)(a)(i)-(iii).

new_rules.legal_concept: Requester self-copying of >50 pages with copy-fee waiver
new_rules.atomic_rule: For a request of more than 50 pages of non-exempt (or segregable) records, an entity may provide copying facilities and require the requester to make the copies, or allow the requester's own copying equipment and personnel on site and waive the copying fees.
new_rules.trigger: Request exceeds 50 pages; records non-exempt or segregable; reasonable safeguards against loss provided
new_rules.source_language: (10)(a) A governmental entity may allow a person requesting more than 50 pages of records to copy the records if: (i) the records are contained in files that do not contain records that are exempt from disclosure, or the records may be segregated to remove private, protected, or controlled information from disclosure; and (ii) the governmental entity provides reasonable safeguards to protect the public from the potential for loss of a public record. (b) If the requirements of Subsection (10)(a) are met, the governmental entity may: (i) provide the requester with the facilities for copying the requested records and require that the requester make the copies; or (ii) allow the requester to provide the requester's own copying facilities and personnel to make the copies at the governmental entity's offices and waive the fees for copying the records.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (63G-2-201 amended 2026 General Session, effective 7/1/2026; fee-related subsections (1)(a), (6), (8)(c), (10) unchanged in substance)
new_rules.notes: Also invoked by § 63G-2-204(7)(c)(iv)(A) for non-expedited voluminous requests. Discretionary; not a free-page allowance.

new_rules.legal_concept: No fee for inspecting a record
new_rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity may not charge a fee for inspecting a record; a person has the right to inspect a public record free of charge.
new_rules.source_language: (5)(b) A governmental entity may not charge a fee for: (i) reviewing a record to determine whether it is subject to disclosure, except as permitted by Subsection (2)(a)(ii); (ii) inspecting a record; or (iii) the first quarter hour of staff time spent in responding to a request under Section 63G-2-204. | § 63G-2-201(1)(a): Except as provided in Subsection (1)(b), a person has the right to inspect a public record free of charge, and the right to take a copy of a public record during normal working hours, subject to Sections 63G-2-203 and 63G-2-204.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (63G-2-203 last amended Ch. 33 (S.B. 188), 2025 General Session, effective 3/17/2025 — technical wording change to (8)(a)(ii) only; no 2026 General Session amendment as of 2026-08-19)
new_rules.notes: May duplicate an Inspection-category row elsewhere in the UT corpus; added here because the fee/payment subset carried only (5)(b)(i) and (5)(b)(iii).

new_rules.legal_concept: Municipal electronic payment acceptance and electronic payment fee
new_rules.atomic_rule: A municipality may accept an electronic payment (credit, charge, debit, prepaid/stored-value card, or ACH) for funds it could receive by another method, and a municipality that accepts electronic payment may charge an electronic payment fee to defray the card company's or processing agent's charges.
new_rules.trigger: Municipality elects to accept electronic payment
new_rules.source_language: (1) As used in this section: (a) "Electronic payment" means the payment of money to a municipality by electronic means, including by means of a credit card, charge card, debit card, prepaid or stored value card or similar device, or automatic clearinghouse transaction. (b) "Electronic payment fee" means an amount of money to defray the discount fee, processing fee, or other fee charged by a credit card company or processing agent to process an electronic payment. (c) "Processing agent" means a bank, transaction clearinghouse, or other third party that charges a fee to process an electronic payment. (2) A municipality may accept an electronic payment for the payment of funds which the municipality could have received through another payment method. (3) A municipality that accepts an electronic payment may charge an electronic payment fee.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (enacted Ch. 29, 2005 General Session; never amended)
new_rules.notes: Not a GRAMA provision; general municipal power. County analogue § 17-15-28.

new_rules.legal_concept: Political-subdivision GRAMA ordinance/policy must carry fee guidelines per § 63G-2-203
new_rules.atomic_rule: A political subdivision's records ordinance or policy shall provide guidelines for establishment of fees in accordance with § 63G-2-203; a political subdivision that does not adopt and maintain an ordinance or policy is subject to the chapter directly.
new_rules.trigger: Political subdivision adopts (or fails to adopt) a GRAMA ordinance/policy
new_rules.source_language: (2)(a) Each political subdivision may adopt an ordinance or a policy applicable throughout its jurisdiction relating to information practices including classification, designation, access, denials, segregation, appeals, management, retention, and amendment of records. (b) The ordinance or policy shall comply with the criteria set forth in this section. (c) If any political subdivision does not adopt and maintain an ordinance or policy, then that political subdivision is subject to this chapter. ... (3) Each ordinance or policy relating to information practices shall: ... (c) provide guidelines for establishment of fees in accordance with Section 63G-2-203;
new_rules.effective_status: Current (63G-2-701 amended Ch. 476, 2025 General Session, effective 5/7/2025)
new_rules.notes: The municipal hook that makes every Utah rate item defers_to_city: the state supplies the actual-cost standard and the process (ordinance/written policy of the governing body, § 63G-2-203(3)(c)); the city supplies the numbers. Note § 63G-2-701(2)(d) enumerates the sections that bind a political subdivision notwithstanding its ordinance and does not list § 63G-2-203 by number, but (3)(c) ties the ordinance's fees to § 63G-2-203 and § 63G-2-201(1)(a) makes the right to copy 'subject to' § 63G-2-203.

applicability_notes: GRAMA's fee section binds every 'governmental entity' — the term includes political subdivisions — so the $50 prepayment trigger, the free first quarter hour, the no-fee-for-review/inspection rules, the lowest-paid-employee hourly cap and the actual-cost standard all bind municipalities directly (§ 63G-2-203; § 63G-2-701(3)(c) ties a city ordinance's fees to § 203).

Every RATE (per-page, media, certification, delivery, A/V, specialty, labor $/hr) is set locally by ordinance or written formal policy of the governing body (§ 63G-2-203(3)(c)) — resolved as defers_to_city (or formula ceiling for labor). State-agency schedules (annual fee acts under § 63J-1-504; e.g., the AG office GRAMA fee schedule) are agency-only and are NOT recorded as municipal values.

§ 63G-2-701(2)(d) lists the sections that bind a political subdivision even if it adopts its own ordinance and omits § 63G-2-203 by number; but § 701(3)(c) requires the ordinance's fee guidelines to be 'in accordance with Section 63G-2-203', § 701(2)(c) subjects a subdivision without an ordinance to the whole chapter, and § 63G-2-201(1)(a) makes copying 'subject to' § 203. Treated as binding on municipalities; flagged for legal review only as to whether a city ordinance could lawfully vary a § 203 numeric parameter (e.g., the $50 trigger).

The Archives official forms (payment/prepayment form; request form) are published for use by any governmental entity; their clock and cost-contact statements are guidance, not law, and are recorded as Official Form rows (UT-9001, UT-9002).
Payment method (UT-9006) comes from the Utah Municipal Code, municipality-specific; counties have a parallel provision (§ 17-15-28).

GRO/State Records Committee fee decisions (e.g., 2024-202 Mullor v. Town of Hideout, 2025) are adjudicative and case-specific; none was found that states an operational fee rule beyond the statute, so none is recorded as a rule.
material_negatives: No statewide per-page copy rate (B&W, color, oversized), specialty, media, delivery, certification or audio/video figure for any Utah public body; the statute names only the actual-cost/reasonable standard and delegates figures to local ordinance/policy.
No graduated page bands, free-page allowance, de-minimis, minimum fee, billing increment, or overhead/fringe percentage.

No estimate-notice threshold, requester response window, revised-estimate percentage, estimate validity period, or overrun re-issue rule; only the $50 prepayment trigger and refund of excess prepayment.
No commercial-purpose fee schedule or surcharge; purpose is relevant only to discretionary waiver, expedited response and the media carve-out.
No fee forfeiture for a late response (late = deemed denial); no per-requestor periodic free-hours budget; no cost-aggregation threshold across requests.

No Utah Administrative Code rule, AG opinion, or records-authority directive sets municipal GRAMA fees; the Government Records Office's rulemaking authority (2025) has not produced a fee rule found in this pass.
